summary: Defines a flag bit in the DNSKEY record to mark a key as a Secure Entry Point (SEP). It helps tell such keys apart from other keys when exchanging keys with the parent and when generating DS records. It updates RFC 2535 and RFC 3755, and was replaced by RFC 4033, RFC 4034 and RFC 4035.

eli5.summary: Some keys act as the front door of a signed zone. This adds a small marker so people know which key is the front-door one.

questions: what is the dnskey sep flag
